verification_method: Python standard-library ElementTree parsed every spectrum; base64 intensity arrays were decoded as little-endian IEEE 754 float32 (all uncompressed) and accumulated with math.fsum. Counts sum spectrum defaultArrayLength and decoded intensity lengths. Source SHA256 was computed from the input bytes.
cache_creation_notes: Installed TOPP FileConverter supports mzML to cachedMzML directly; no OpenSWATH package or other tool is required. It writes both the cached binary and the corresponding metadata mzML. Cache creation is preprocessing and must be timed/reported separately and excluded from TIC read timings. No cache has been created by this review.
recommended_run_arguments: <mzML, or matching cachedMzML for cached methods>
method_caveats: Run benchmark processes serially after test execution ends to avoid test/benchmark contention. Report warm-cache Debug measurements, median/min/max external wall time including process startup, and exact build identity.
Set -threads explicitly to 1 and 2: TOPPBase sets its own OpenMP thread count, with a default of 1.
TICCalculator main ignores the return value of tool.main() and returns 0; require valid spectrum count, peak count and TIC output and reject error diagnostics in addition to checking process status.

TICCalculator prints TIC using default stream precision (six significant digits); compare the printed value against the corresponding precision of the independently decoded TIC rather than claiming full precision numeric equality.
indexed_parallel skips metadata loading and XML checks unlike indexed, so differences between these methods are not exclusively parallel speedup.
cached and cached_parallel always decode the cached data and ignore loadData=false; keep loadData=true in all modes.
Tool-reported memory is sampled resident size in KiB, not process peak RSS. Use external per-process peak RSS measurement for peak-memory comparisons.
Only spectra contribute to TICCalculator counts and ion current; chromatograms are ignored.
TICCalculator automatically appends -test, which suppresses usage reporting.
The 13 MB input is a bounded regression-data workload, not a full-scale proteomics acquisition or Release performance qualification.
